So, there are a whole host of problems with this video, but to start from the end, the notion that history classes do
not teach Jesus as a historical figure is pure and utter nonsense. That is bafflingly ignorant. Virtually any
history class you could ever take in any university or college or even high school in the United States of America
is going to teach Jesus as a historical figure to the degree that history class even addresses Jesus. Now, there's a
distinction between the historical Jesus that scholars try to reconstruct from the available data and the supernatural
son of God, Messiah of the Gospels and the rest of the New Testament who came back from the dead and walked on water and gave sight to the blind.
And the notion that the number of manuscripts that we have for specifically biographical texts about
these figures is somehow determinative of the historicity of the figure that is
addressed in those biographical texts is so laughably uninformed as to betray just an abject and a total ignorance of
how historical criticism works. The number of manuscripts is utterly
unrelated to the historicity of a historical figure. It's not how many times a specific text was copied that determines historicity.
We have to look at what's in the text and then we have to compare that to all the available data of whatever type.
Whether that is letters from the ancient world or inscriptions or bulli or numismatic evidence or archaeological
data related to battles and places that the person was supposed to have stayed or lived or done something. We look at artistic evidence. We look at statuary.
We look at other historical narratives that provide context for what's going on here and can tell us whether or not the
narratives in the biographical texts actually fit or do not fit those contexts. We look at everything that
could possibly provide context and point in the direction of historicity or ahistoricity and then we try to come up
with the best way to account for how the data got to be the way they are. And when it comes to folks like Julius
Caesar, we have so many other types of data that pointed in the direction of historicity that are far stronger than
a biography written by someone who was not alive when Julius Caesar was alive.
But that biography provides a lot of data that can then be correlated to what we do have from the time period of the
life of Julius Caesar. There are so many different things that go into determining historicity and the number
